name: Pancit Canton
description: A beloved stir-fried wheat noodle dish tossed with mixed vegetables and your choice of meat or seafood in a savory soy-based sauce.
culturalNote: Long noodles like canton are traditionally served at Filipino birthdays and celebrations, symbolizing a long life.

name: Pancit Bihon
description: A light, savory dish of thin rice noodles stir-fried with julienned vegetables, meat, and a touch of soy sauce.
culturalNote: One of the most common pancit variations found in homes and gatherings across the Philippines.

name: Pancit Malabon
description: Thick rice noodles bathed in a rich, orange-hued shrimp sauce and generously topped with seafood and vegetables.
culturalNote: Named after Malabon City, a coastal community known for its abundant seafood.

name: Pancit Palabok
description: Rice noodles covered in a savory shrimp and annatto sauce, topped with crushed chicharrón, shrimp, egg, and scallions.
culturalNote: A festive favorite often prepared for fiestas and special family occasions.

name: Pancit Batil Patung
description: A hearty noodle dish from Tuguegarao, topped with a cracked fried egg ("batil") and a ladle of flavorful beef broth and toppings ("patung").
culturalNote: A signature street-food dish of the Cagayan Valley, often sold by vendors called 'miki houses'.

name: Pancit Habhab
description: A Lucban specialty traditionally served on a banana leaf and eaten utensil-free, straight from the leaf — a style known as 'habhab'.
culturalNote: The 'habhab' eating style is a playful Lucban tradition said to have started among students in a hurry between classes.

name: Pancit Lomi
description: A hearty, thick egg-noodle soup simmered in a starchy pork or chicken broth — comforting on any rainy day.
culturalNote: A Batangas comfort food enjoyed as a warm snack or meal, especially during cooler weather.

name: Pancit Molo
description: A savory dumpling soup inspired by Chinese wonton soup, featuring delicate meat-filled dumplings in a clear, flavorful broth.
culturalNote: Named after the Molo district of Iloilo City, reflecting the area's long history of Chinese-Filipino cuisine.
